title: Metallic Néel order stabilized by coupling between inequivalent Hubbard layers
authors: Yi-Ming Wu, Jessica Yiqi Pan, Hong Yao, Steven A. Kivelson
abstract: Inspired by recent ARPES studies on multilayer ($n\geq3$ layers) cuprate superconductors, we use the unrestricted Hartree-Fock approximation to explore the ground-state phase diagram of two coupled, inequivalently doped square-lattice Hubbard layers. In the decoupled-layer limit, the lightly hole-doped ground state is typically an incommensurate spin-stripe state. However, with sufficiently strong interlayer coupling, stripe order is destabilized relative to a commensurate Néel-ordered metal. The resulting state exhibits a reconstructed Fermi surface with hole pockets centered at $(\pmπ/2,\pmπ/2)$ that are similar in character to those seen in experiments. Our results illustrate the qualitatively new physics that can arise from interlayer coupling in multilayer cuprates.
summary: This theoretical work models multilayer cuprates using the Hubbard Hamiltonian to determine the ground-state magnetic order. It finds that interlayer coupling stabilizes a commensurate Néel-ordered metal phase, overcoming the tendency toward incommensurate spin-stripe order seen in isolated layers. This provides a crucial theoretical insight into the complex interplay between dimensionality and magnetic order in high-temperature superconductors.
main_problem: The study investigates how interlayer coupling influences the magnetic ground state in lightly hole-doped multilayer cuprates, specifically contrasting the tendency toward incommensurate spin-stripe order with the stabilization of a commensurate Néel-ordered metal.
main_result: The interlayer coupling is shown to destabilize the stripe order relative to a commensurate Néel-ordered metal, leading to a reconstructed Fermi surface consistent with experimental observations in cuprates.
method: The research employs the unrestricted Hartree-Fock approximation to map the ground-state phase diagram of the coupled Hubbard layers.
model_or_system: The model consists of two coupled, inequivalently doped square-lattice Hubbard layers, described by a Hamiltonian including hopping terms ($t, t', t_\perp$) and on-site repulsion ($U$).
key_observables: Phase diagram mapping, site-dependent spin densities, and spectral function analysis to distinguish between Néel and stripe order.
important_parameters: Doping ($\delta$), interlayer hopping ($t_\perp/t$), and the ratio of interaction strength to hopping ($U/t$).
main_assumptions: The use of the unrestricted Hartree-Fock approximation, which is assumed reliable at weak to intermediate Hubbard interaction strengths.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate single-layer and bilayer phase diagrams showing transitions between various ordered phases (Néel, stripe) and metallic states as doping and coupling strength change.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the phase diagram by first considering the decoupled limit ($t_\perp=0$), then introducing interlayer coupling ($t_\perp>0$) to show the stabilization of the commensurate Néel state over the stripe state.
why_interesting: The mechanism of stabilizing a commensurate magnetic order via interlayer coupling in a strongly correlated system is a key theoretical concept relevant to understanding high-Tc superconductivity mechanisms.
